- Overestimate prices in the short term after positive sentiment spikes; model tends to overshoot early in the 30-day horizon.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or neutral, especially in the first 7–10 days of the forecast window.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overreacts to recent spikes, then undercorrects in subsequent days.
- When sentiment turns sharply negative (e.g., -1.25+), model fails to adjust downward quickly; forecast remains high for 3–5 days.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag: true price often exceeds forecast by 0.5–2.0 units in the 15–25 day range, especially after sentiment shifts.
- Model underestimates late-period (25–30d) prices when sentiment is positive and trending upward — overconfidence in short-term momentum.
- Avoid extrapolating sentiment trends beyond 3–5 days; sentiment decay often causes model to overcorrect or misalign with true price behavior.
